key_insight: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA) is a model-agnostic orchestration framework that separates oncology data routing from AI inference to make clinical decision support more flexible and scalable.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals integrate multimodal cancer data and swap AI models without rebuilding the whole decision-support pipeline.
method: Formalized as a 7-tuple architecture with "Algorithmic Impermeability" to keep orchestration independent of the AI model.
Uses an "Entry Theory" and Geometric Deep Learning to standardize multimodal patient data across structural and medical axes.
Routes data through a Cancer Switching Module and outputs a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP) for downstream use.
evidence_signal: A proof-of-concept tested four technical scenarios, showing negligible orchestration overhead, stable routing during model swaps, and 100% recall for targeted supplementary data requests under injected anomalies.
watch_item: The framework was validated only in a proof-of-concept setting, so real-world integration with hospital IT systems and EMRs still needs careful testing.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
